Redwood Inference — Enterprise Security FAQ v2 (DRAFT)
Owner: Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance PM)
Last edited: 2026-02-06
Status: Draft for cross-functional review (Security Eng + GRC + Product + Solutions Eng)

DO NOT SEND EXTERNALLY YET.
This draft includes: unresolved questions, placeholders for evidence links, and tracked-edits style notes inline.

Audience
- Primary: prospect/customer security reviewers, IT/security teams
- Secondary: AEs/SEs needing approved language for questionnaires

How to use (internal)
- If the customer asks for “proof” (SOC 2 report, pen test summary, subprocessor list), do NOT attach directly unless you’ve followed the evidence sharing process.
- Route evidence requests to GRC: Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter.
- For claims with legal implications (incident notification timelines, liability), route to Legal: Michael Grant / Sofia Mendes.

Canonical version
- Source of truth will be Confluence page “Enterprise Security FAQ v2” once approved.
- This Drive doc is working draft; some wording is intentionally cautious.

====================
1) Quick overview / scope
====================

Q1. What is Redwood Inference?
A. Redwood Inference is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing large language model (LLM) inference across:
- Hosted API
- Dedicated capacity
- Private deployments (customer VPC and on-prem options)

Q2. What deployment modes do you offer and what is the shared responsibility model?
A. Responsibilities vary by deployment mode:

Hosted API
- Redwood operates and secures the infrastructure and service.
- Customer configures access (API keys / SSO), usage policies, and customer-side application security.

Dedicated
- Redwood operates dedicated GPU capacity allocated to a single customer (data isolation at the capacity layer).
- Shared responsibility is similar to Hosted, with additional controls/contractual options depending on architecture.

Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Redwood provides the software and support; the customer controls their network environment and many operational controls.
- Exact boundary depends on whether the control plane is customer-managed and how telemetry/log forwarding is configured.

[TODO: Add diagram reference once ENG-23310 public docs snippet is finalized]
Placeholder: [LINK: Deployment Modes — Security Boundary (public doc) — TBD]

EDIT NOTE (Markus Klein, SE): Keep this crisp; security reviewers want a clear boundary. Add a “who patches what” callout for Private.

====================
2) Compliance & assurance
====================

Q3. Do you have SOC 2?
A. Redwood Inference maintains a SOC 2 report. We can share the SOC 2 report under NDA via our controlled evidence sharing process.

Evidence pointer (internal):
- [EVIDENCE: SOC 2 report + bridge letter (if applicable) — request via GRC]
- [PROCESS: Customer Security Review Process (internal) — Confluence link TBD]

EDIT NOTE (Olga Petrov, GRC): Avoid stating “SOC 2 Type II” in this draft until we confirm exact report language for this cycle. Use “SOC 2 report” in external-facing copy.

Q4. Do you support customer security questionnaires?
A. Yes. We aim to respond to security questionnaires promptly. For complex requests (evidence sharing, custom contractual language, deep architecture questions), we coordinate with Security/GRC and, when required, Legal.

Internal routing:
- Standard answers: use the RFP response library
- Evidence: GRC
- Contract language: Legal

Placeholder: [LINK: Standard RFP Response Library — TBD]

Q5. Do you conduct penetration tests and vulnerability assessments?
A. We perform ongoing security testing and vulnerability management as part of our secure development lifecycle. We can share high-level summaries of relevant assessments under NDA when appropriate.

Evidence pointer (internal):
- [EVIDENCE: Pen test summary (NDA) — request via GRC]

EDIT NOTE (Marcus Lin, Security Eng): Do not promise a specific pen test frequency in customer-facing docs; frequency may vary by scope and vendor.

====================
3) Data handling: prompts, outputs, and customer content
====================

Q6. Does Redwood train models on customer prompts/outputs?
A. By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts or model outputs to train foundation models.

EDIT NOTE (Naomi): Keep “foundation models” phrasing; confirm whether any opt-in product analytics includes sampled content. If any sampling exists, must be explicitly described + configurable.

OPEN QUESTION (Product): Are there any support workflows that request customers to provide example prompts/outputs? If yes, add “only when customer shares for support/debugging” language.

Q7. Who owns the customer data processed by Redwood?
A. Customers retain ownership of their data. Redwood processes customer data as needed to provide the service, per contractual terms.

Q8. Do you have a DPA and subprocessors list?
A. Redwood can provide a DPA and subprocessor information for customers as part of security/procurement review.

Evidence pointer (internal):
- [EVIDENCE: DPA template / Legal process — request via Legal]
- [EVIDENCE: Subprocessor list (customer-facing) — request via GRC]

EDIT NOTE (Legal - Michael Grant): Do not state “we will sign any customer DPA.” Say “we can provide a DPA” and route exceptions.

====================
4) Data residency & regional controls
====================

Q9. Where is customer data processed? Do you support data residency?
A. Data processing location depends on deployment mode and region selection.
- Hosted/Dedicated: customers may select from available regions for request processing (subject to product availability).
- Private: processing occurs within the customer’s environment (VPC/on-prem), subject to the customer’s infrastructure choices.

For detailed region availability and how logs/telemetry may be handled by mode, see the Data Residency one-pager.

Placeholder: [LINK: Data Residency one-pager — TBD]

OPEN QUESTION (GRC): Confirm exact list of regions that are “GA” vs “by request,” and ensure we don’t over-commit on EU-only processing if some telemetry is centralized.

Q10. Do you support restricting data to the EU?
A. Redwood can support EU-based processing where EU regions are available. Specific configurations and any exceptions (e.g., operational telemetry) should be confirmed during the security review based on your deployment mode and support plan.

EDIT NOTE (Lukas Meyer, EMEA Sales): We need a tight answer here; “telemetry exceptions” causes concern. Provide specifics in the data residency one-pager and link to it.

====================
5) Data retention, deletion, and logging retention
====================

Q11. What is your default data retention for prompts and outputs?
A. Retention depends on the product configuration and deployment mode.
- Hosted/Dedicated: operational data retention may apply for service delivery, security, and troubleshooting. Some retention settings may be configurable depending on plan and features enabled.
- Private: retention is primarily controlled by the customer’s environment and logging configuration.

For current defaults and available controls, see the Data Retention Controls one-pager.

Placeholder: [LINK: Data Retention Controls one-pager — TBD]

EDIT NOTE (Kevin Osei): We must be precise on what’s retained vs not retained: prompts/outputs vs metadata vs audit logs. Avoid “we don’t store prompts” unless confirmed across all routes + configs.

Q12. Can customers request deletion of their data?
A. Yes. Customers can request deletion in accordance with the contract and applicable law. Process and timelines may vary by data type and deployment mode.

====================
6) Encryption & key management
====================

Q13. Is customer data encrypted in transit?
A. Redwood uses encryption in transit for service communications using industry-standard protocols.

EDIT NOTE (Marcus Lin): Avoid “all traffic” / “always” phrasing; say “uses TLS for service communications” and link to security overview once published.

Q14. Is customer data encrypted at rest?
A. For Hosted and Dedicated, Redwood uses encryption at rest for applicable storage systems used by the service.
For Private, encryption at rest depends on the customer’s infrastructure and configuration.

Q15. Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A. Options vary by deployment mode:
- Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood supports standard cloud key management patterns; customer-managed key options may be available for certain enterprise configurations.
- Private: customers can integrate their own KMS/HSM depending on their environment.

OPEN QUESTION (Private SME - Colin O’Donnell): Confirm which key management integrations are supported in VPC Private today vs roadmap. Need a “current state” section and a separate “roadmap (if asked)” script.

====================
7) Identity, SSO, and access controls
====================

Q16. Do you support SSO (SAML) for the Redwood Console?
A. Redwood supports SSO for enterprise customers. Details (IdP compatibility, SAML configuration) are available in the SSO/SAML one-pager.

Placeholder: [LINK: SSO/SAML one-pager — TBD]

Q17. Do you support SCIM provisioning?
A. [DRAFT ANSWER — needs confirmation]
- If supported: Redwood supports SCIM for automated user provisioning for the Console.
- If not supported / limited: Redwood is evaluating/expanding automated provisioning options; customers can manage access via admin controls and role-based access.

OPEN QUESTION (Auth SME - Ethan Park): Confirm SCIM status across Hosted/Dedicated/Private control planes. If partial support, define exactly what is supported (users, groups, deprovisioning).

Q18. Do you have RBAC?
A. Yes. Redwood provides role-based access control (RBAC) for the Console and administrative functions.

Placeholder: [LINK: RBAC model reference — TBD]

EDIT NOTE (Markus Klein): Security reviewers often ask “can I prevent developers from viewing prompts?” If not possible today, say so clearly and offer compensating controls (Private, customer-side encryption, app-layer controls).

Q19. How are API keys managed?
A. Redwood supports API keys for programmatic access. Customers should store keys securely, rotate keys per internal policy, and restrict distribution. Enterprise options may include centralized access management via SSO and RBAC for Console operations.

====================
8) Audit logging & monitoring
====================

Q20. Do you provide audit logs?
A. Redwood provides audit logging for relevant administrative and platform events. Audit log coverage depends on deployment mode and enabled features.

For the current set of events and export options, see the Audit Logging Overview one-pager.

Placeholder: [LINK: Audit Logging Overview one-pager — TBD]

EDIT NOTE (Kevin Osei): We need to list categories (auth events, API key changes, user/role changes, org settings, model deployments/rollouts) but avoid enumerating exact event names unless we can keep it updated.

Q21. Can audit logs be exported to a SIEM?
A. Export options vary. We can support common enterprise logging workflows; specific mechanisms depend on deployment mode and customer requirements.

OPEN QUESTION (Security Eng): Confirm current export mechanism wording (push vs pull, webhook vs periodic export). Do not imply real-time streaming if it’s batch today.

====================
9) Application security, SDLC, and vulnerability management
====================

Q22. Do you have a secure development lifecycle (SDLC)?
A. Redwood follows a secure development lifecycle that includes code review, CI/CD controls, and vulnerability management.

Placeholder: [LINK: Secure SDLC summary one-pager — TBD]

Q23. How do you handle vulnerability remediation?
A. Redwood prioritizes and remediates vulnerabilities based on severity and risk. Timelines may vary based on scope and impact.

EDIT NOTE (Olga Petrov): If we include remediation SLAs, they must match the customer-facing Secure SDLC summary and any contractual commitments.

====================
10) Incident response & customer notification
====================

Q24. Do you have an incident response program?
A. Yes. Redwood maintains incident response processes for detecting, triaging, and remediating security incidents.

Placeholder: [LINK: Incident Response & Notification one-pager — TBD]

Q25. How and when do you notify customers of security incidents?
A. Redwood will notify customers of a confirmed security incident involving their data in accordance with contractual terms and applicable law. Notification timing and method may depend on incident scope and contract.

TRACKED-EDITS NOTE (from Sales thread): Several AEs want a simple “we notify within X hours.” Security/GRC recommends avoiding hard numbers unless in contract. Provide “without undue delay” language and point to contract/SLA.

OPEN QUESTION (Legal): Confirm if we can say “without undue delay” or if we should use more neutral “in accordance with contract.”

Q26. Do you have a public status page?
A. Redwood provides service status updates through established support channels. For major service disruptions, customers may receive direct communications depending on plan.

OPEN QUESTION (Support/CS): Confirm whether there is a public status page vs private status communications. Avoid linking to something that doesn’t exist.

====================
11) Privacy, confidentiality, and employee access
====================

Q27. Do Redwood employees have access to customer data?
A. Access to customer systems and data is restricted and controlled. Access may be granted for operational support or troubleshooting when necessary, consistent with policy and contractual terms.

EDIT NOTE (GRC): We should mention least privilege and logging of administrative access, but do not claim “no one can access” since support access exists.

====================
12) Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) specifics
====================

Q28. For Private (VPC), can Redwood access the customer environment?
A. Private deployments are designed to run within customer-controlled environments. Support access patterns vary by implementation (e.g., customer-managed bastion, break-glass procedures, or customer-provided logs). Specific access arrangements are defined during deployment and in the support plan.

EDIT NOTE (Private reviewer - Vivek Kulkarni): Emphasize customer control; do not imply Redwood has persistent access.

Q29. For on-prem / air-gapped environments, can you operate without external connectivity?
A. Some Private deployments may be configured for restricted connectivity depending on requirements. Feasibility depends on the operational model (updates, monitoring, and support processes).

OPEN QUESTION (Private/Regulated - Fatima Noor): Define minimum connectivity requirements for standard Private vs regulated/on-prem package. Provide a standard “it depends” answer + escalation path.

====================
13) Support, SLAs, and escalation
====================

Q30. What support options and SLAs are available?
A. Support levels and SLAs vary by plan and contract (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Enterprise customers may have defined response targets and escalation paths.

15) Drafting notes / open issues tracker (internal)
====================

High-risk wording to finalize in Week 2–3
1) Data retention defaults (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — need exact language + ensure consistent with one-pager.
2) Audit log scope — what’s logged today vs roadmap; avoid “everything is logged.”
3) Incident notification — avoid hard timelines unless contract; confirm Legal-approved phrasing.
4) Data residency — confirm EU region posture and telemetry/log flows.
5) SCIM — confirm support status.

Questions from field feedback to address (from AEs/SEs)
- “Do you store prompts/outputs?” (need precise answer)
- “Can you guarantee my data never leaves X region?” (need shared responsibility + exceptions clarity)
- “Can admins restrict who can view prompts in Console?” (need truth + compensating controls)
- “Can we get a single link to the latest kit?” (packaging/permissions; likely Confluence canonical + Drive PDFs)
